|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Complete the capstone project by evaluating the fine-tuned model against the base model and iterating based on observed weaknesses.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Teacher explanation** | Part 2 completes the project by applying Lecture 475's evaluation methodology and Lecture 476's overfitting diagnostics to your own part-1 adapter: run both the base model and your fine-tuned adapter on your held-out validation set, score the outputs against your task-specific criteria, and separately test a handful of general-purpose prompts to check for catastrophic forgetting as covered in Lecture 479. Based on what this evaluation reveals, iterate deliberately rather than randomly -- if validation loss diverged from training loss, address overfitting (fewer epochs, more data, lower rank); if general-capability regressions appeared, consider mixing in general instruction examples or reducing training intensity; if the task-specific accuracy simply isn't high enough yet, consider whether the dataset needs more diverse examples rather than just more training time. The project concludes with a short written comparison: base model versus fine-tuned model performance on the target task, any regressions observed, and what you would do differently with more time or data, which mirrors the kind of adaptation-decision writeup a real engineering team would produce before deciding whether to deploy a fine-tuned model. This habit of honest, structured before-and-after comparison -- not just celebrating a lower loss number -- is the single most transferable skill from this entire project. |
| **Worked example**      | After evaluating their formal-email adapter, a learner finds it scores well on the target task (38 of 40 validation examples preferred over base model output) but shows a slight regression on 2 of 10 general prompts, so they retrain with a small amount of general instruction data mixed in and re-evaluate before finalizing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

**Knowledge check:** What should drive the iteration choices made in part 2 of the project?

\(A\) Random hyperparameter changes made without reference to the evaluation results

**(B) Specific weaknesses revealed by the evaluation -- such as overfitting signs or general-capability regressions -- each addressed with a matching, targeted fix**

\(C\) Always increasing the number of training epochs regardless of what evaluation shows

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Complete part 2 of your project: evaluate your fine-tuned adapter against the base model on your validation set and on 5 general prompts, make at least one targeted iteration based on the results, and write a 5-8 sentence comparison summary.

**Lecture 483 Fine-tuning and PEFT in context: a project retrospective**

*Year 3 · Month 28 · Fine-Tuning + PEFT · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Synthesize the month's concepts by articulating, for your own completed project, which decisions mattered most and why.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Teacher explanation** | This retrospective lecture asks you to step back from the mechanics of LoRA, dataset preparation, and evaluation, and instead articulate the decision chain that shaped your project: why fine-tuning was the right tool for your chosen task rather than prompting or RAG (Lecture 469), why you chose the base model size you did (Lecture 480), and what your evaluation results actually told you about whether the fine-tune was worth its cost. This kind of retrospective is standard practice on real ML teams before a fine-tuned model goes anywhere near production, because the technical mechanics of LoRA are the easy part compared to justifying, in plain language a non-technical stakeholder could follow, why this specific approach was chosen and what tradeoffs were accepted. Write your retrospective as if explaining the project to a manager deciding whether to approve further investment: state the task, the decision to fine-tune, the model size and PEFT method chosen and why, the evaluation results including any limitations or regressions found, and a clear recommendation on whether this approach is ready to deploy, needs more work, or should be abandoned in favor of a different approach entirely. This is also the right moment to honestly note where your 150-300 example dataset is smaller than what a production system would likely need, and what scaling it up would require. |
| **Worked example**      | A learner's retrospective states: 'I chose fine-tuning over RAG because the task was about consistent tone, not facts; I used a 1B model because latency mattered more than maximum accuracy; evaluation showed 38/40 wins on-task with a minor regression on 2 general prompts, which I partially fixed; I'd recommend this for a pilot but would want 3x more training data before full deployment.'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Knowledge check:** What is the primary purpose of writing a project retrospective in plain, stakeholder-facing language rather than purely technical notes?

\(A\) To replace the need for any technical documentation of the project

**(B) To practice justifying technical tradeoffs and decisions in a way a non-technical stakeholder deciding on further investment could actually follow**

\(C\) Retrospectives have no practical value once a project's code runs correctly

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Write a 150-250 word retrospective of your capstone project in the stakeholder-facing style described, covering the fine-tune decision, model choice, evaluation results, and a clear recommendation.

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Explain conceptually how a vision transformer processes an image differently than the convolutional networks covered in Year 2 Month 19.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Teacher explanation** | Year 2 Month 19 covered convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which process an image through local filters sliding across pixel neighborhoods, building up features from small local patterns toward larger ones. A vision transformer (ViT) takes a fundamentally different approach: it slices an image into a grid of fixed-size patches (for example 16x16 pixels each), flattens and embeds each patch into a vector much like a word becomes a token embedding in a language transformer, and then feeds the full sequence of patch embeddings through the same self-attention mechanism used in text transformers, letting every patch attend to every other patch regardless of spatial distance. This global attention is the key conceptual difference from CNNs: where a CNN builds up long-range understanding gradually through many stacked local layers, a ViT can relate a patch in the top-left corner to a patch in the bottom-right corner in a single attention step, which can capture certain long-range visual relationships more directly, at the cost of needing much more training data to learn the spatial structure that a CNN gets built-in through its convolutional design. In practice, many of today's strongest vision and multimodal systems use ViT-style image encoders precisely because the same transformer architecture can then integrate naturally with a language model, which is the architectural foundation for the vision-language models covered later this month. |
| **Worked example**      | A ViT processing a 224x224 image might split it into 196 patches of 16x16 pixels each, embed each patch as a vector, and let self-attention directly relate a patch showing a dog's ear to a patch showing its tail in one computation step, rather than building that relationship up gradually through many convolutional layers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Knowledge check:** What is the key conceptual difference between how a CNN and a vision transformer build understanding of long-range relationships in an image?

\(A\) CNNs and vision transformers use mathematically identical mechanisms with no meaningful difference

**(B) A CNN builds long-range understanding gradually through stacked local convolutional layers, while a ViT's self-attention can relate distant patches directly in a single step**

\(C\) Vision transformers cannot process images larger than a single pixel

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Write 4-5 sentences comparing, for a specific image you choose, how a CNN versus a ViT would conceptually build up an understanding of a relationship between two distant objects in that image.

**Lecture 486 What "multimodal" means for a model**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Define multimodality precisely and distinguish models that process multiple modalities from models that only generate across them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Teacher explanation** | A multimodal model is one that can take in, and often also produce, information across more than one modality -- commonly text, images, and increasingly audio or video -- within a single unified system, rather than requiring separate specialized models stitched together by hand for each modality. It's important to distinguish different multimodal capabilities precisely: some models are multimodal on input only (they can understand an image alongside text but only generate text output, as in many vision-language models), while others are multimodal on both input and output (they can both understand and generate images, as in text-to-image and increasingly unified generation models), and conflating these two capabilities leads to real confusion about what a given system can actually do. The practical significance of true multimodality, as opposed to a simple pipeline of separate single-modality models glued together with handoffs, is that a genuinely multimodal model can reason jointly across modalities within one forward pass -- for instance directly relating a specific visual detail in an image to a specific claim in an accompanying text passage -- rather than losing information at each handoff between separate single-modality systems. This joint reasoning capability is precisely what enables the document-understanding and multimodal RAG use cases this month builds toward, where a system must relate layout, embedded images, and text within the same document simultaneously. |
| **Worked example**      | A model that can look at a photo of a receipt and answer 'what was the total amount' in text is multimodal on input (image plus text in) but not on output (only text out), distinct from a model that could also generate a new image of a modified receipt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

**Knowledge check:** Why does true joint multimodal reasoning within one model matter more than a pipeline of separate single-modality models glued together?

\(A\) Pipelines of separate models are always faster and more accurate than any unified model

**(B) A single multimodal model can relate specific details across modalities within one forward pass, avoiding information loss at handoffs between separate pipeline stages**

\(C\) Multimodality has no practical effect on reasoning quality

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Find and describe one real multimodal AI product you've used or seen, stating clearly whether it is multimodal on input only, output only, or both.

**Lecture 487 How a vision-language model combines an image encoder with a language model**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Explain the architectural pattern connecting a vision encoder's output to a language model's input in a vision-language model (VLM).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Teacher explanation** | A vision-language model is typically built by taking a pretrained vision encoder (often a ViT, as covered in Lecture 485) that converts an image into a sequence of feature vectors, and a pretrained language model that processes sequences of token embeddings, then connecting the two with a projection layer that maps the vision encoder's output vectors into the same embedding space the language model expects for its own tokens. Once projected, the image's feature vectors are simply inserted into the language model's input sequence alongside the text token embeddings -- functionally, the language model sees a mixed sequence of 'image tokens' and 'text tokens' and processes them together through its usual self-attention layers, which is what allows the model to relate a specific word in a text prompt to a specific region of the image. Training such a model typically happens in stages: the vision encoder and language model are often each pretrained separately first (on huge single-modality datasets), and then the projection layer (and sometimes parts of the language model) are trained on paired image-text data to teach the combination to align the two modalities meaningfully, which is far more data- and compute-efficient than training a multimodal model entirely from scratch. This modular combine-and-align approach is why so many different VLMs can be built relatively quickly by pairing various existing vision encoders with various existing language models, rather than each lab needing to train a fully new architecture from the ground up. |
| **Worked example**      | A VLM answering 'what color is the car' sees a sequence like \[image_token_1, image_token_2, ..., image_token_196, "what", "color", "is", "the", "car"\] all flowing through the same self-attention layers, letting the language model directly attend to the image tokens most relevant to the word 'car'.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

**Knowledge check:** What is the role of the projection layer in a typical vision-language model architecture?

\(A\) It discards the image entirely and relies only on a text caption

**(B) It maps the vision encoder's output vectors into the same embedding space the language model expects, so image and text tokens can be processed together**

\(C\) It converts the language model's text output into a new image

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Diagram or describe in 4-5 sentences the data flow in a VLM answering a question about an image, labeling where the vision encoder, projection layer, and language model each act.

**Lecture 488 Image captioning and visual question answering as tasks**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Distinguish image captioning and visual question answering (VQA) as distinct multimodal tasks with different evaluation expectations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Teacher explanation** | Image captioning is the task of generating a free-form natural-language description of an image's content, typically without any specific question to answer -- the model's job is simply to describe what's notably present, and good captions balance completeness (covering the salient objects and actions) against concision (not listing every irrelevant detail). Visual question answering (VQA) is a related but distinct task: given an image and a specific natural-language question about it, the model must produce an answer grounded in the image's actual content, which demands more targeted visual reasoning than captioning since the model must identify exactly which visual details are relevant to the specific question asked, rather than describing everything broadly. The two tasks also differ in how they're evaluated: captioning quality is often judged on coverage and fluency (sometimes with automated text-similarity metrics against reference captions, though these are imperfect proxies for true quality), while VQA is more often judged on strict answer correctness, since a VQA answer is usually a short, checkable fact rather than an open-ended description. In practice, VQA is the harder test of genuine visual grounding, because a model can produce a plausible-sounding generic caption without truly attending to the specific image, but a VQA system that gets specific counting, color, or spatial-relationship questions right has demonstrated it actually processed the relevant visual details correctly. |
| **Worked example**      | Given a photo of a kitchen counter, an image-captioning model might produce "A kitchen counter with fruit, a cutting board, and a knife," while a VQA model answering "how many apples are on the counter" must correctly count the specific apples visible, a much narrower and more checkable task.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

**Knowledge check:** Why is VQA generally considered a harder test of genuine visual grounding than captioning?

\(A\) VQA always uses longer input images than captioning

**(B) A caption can sound plausible without precisely attending to specific details, while a VQA answer to a specific question is a short, checkable fact that exposes whether the model actually processed the relevant visual detail**

\(C\) Captioning and VQA use identical evaluation criteria with no meaningful difference

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Find an image and write both a caption for it and 3 VQA-style questions with their correct answers, noting which of the 3 questions would be hardest for a model to answer correctly and why.

**Lecture 489 Document understanding: layout, text, and visuals together**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Explain how document understanding systems combine layout structure, extracted text, and embedded visuals to extract structured information, building on Year 1's OCR concept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Teacher explanation** | Year 1 introduced OCR (optical character recognition) as the task of extracting raw text from an image of a document, but real-world document understanding requires much more than recognized text alone: a document's meaning often depends critically on its layout -- which text is a heading, which is a table cell, which column a number belongs to -- and may include embedded charts, logos, or photos whose content also matters for correctly extracting structured information. Modern document-understanding models combine three signals jointly: the textual content (from OCR or direct text extraction), the spatial layout (the position and size of each text region, table structure, and visual element on the page), and the visual appearance of non-text elements, feeding all three into a single model so that, for instance, a number's meaning can be correctly interpreted based on which labeled table column and row it visually sits in, not just its raw character content. This matters enormously for practical tasks like extracting line items from an invoice, reading values from a multi-column financial table, or pulling specific fields from a form, where the same piece of text can mean completely different things depending on its layout position, and a text-only extraction pipeline that ignores layout will frequently misattribute values to the wrong field or row. Document-understanding systems built this way are a direct, practical application of the vision-language architecture from Lecture 487, since they must jointly reason over an image of the page and the text it contains. |
| **Worked example**      | A document-understanding model extracting data from an invoice correctly attributes the number "\$45.00" to the "Unit Price" column of a specific line item, not the "Quantity" or "Total" column, because it reasons over the table's visual layout alongside the raw OCR text, not the text alone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Knowledge check:** Why does layout matter in document understanding beyond what plain OCR text extraction provides?

\(A\) Layout has no effect on how a number or label should be interpreted

**(B) The same text can mean different things depending on its position in a table or form, so layout must be reasoned over jointly with text content to correctly attribute values to the right field**

\(C\) OCR already fully captures layout information with no additional processing needed

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Find a real document with a table (an invoice, receipt, or form) and write out, for 3 specific values in it, how its position in the layout determines its correct meaning versus just reading the raw extracted text.

**Lecture 490 Multimodal RAG: retrieving images and document pages**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Extend Month 26's RAG concepts to retrieve relevant images and document pages, not just text chunks, for grounding a multimodal answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Teacher explanation** | Month 26 covered retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for text: embedding text chunks, storing them in a vector database, and retrieving the most relevant chunks for a query. Multimodal RAG extends this same core idea to visual content: images, document pages, charts, and diagrams can also be embedded into a shared vector space (often using a multimodal embedding model trained so that semantically related images and text land near each other), stored in a vector database just like text chunks, and retrieved based on similarity to a user's query, even when the query is purely text and the relevant content is primarily visual. A common and practically important pattern is retrieving whole document pages as images rather than just extracted text chunks, which preserves the layout and visual context from Lecture 489 that a text-only extraction would have thrown away -- this matters especially for documents where tables, charts, or diagrams carry meaning that doesn't survive being flattened into plain text. Once relevant images or pages are retrieved, they're passed into a vision-language model alongside the user's query, exactly as in Lecture 487's architecture, so the final generation step can directly reason over the actual retrieved visual content rather than a lossy text summary of it -- this combination of multimodal retrieval and multimodal generation is precisely what powers the multimodal document assistant project later this month. |
| **Worked example**      | A user asks "what was Q3 revenue according to the chart on page 12," and a multimodal RAG system retrieves page 12 as an image (preserving the chart's visual structure), then passes that image plus the question into a VLM to read the specific value directly off the chart.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

**Knowledge check:** Why might multimodal RAG retrieve a whole document page as an image rather than just its extracted text?

\(A\) Retrieving images is always computationally free compared to text

**(B) Retrieving the page as an image preserves layout, tables, and chart content that a text-only extraction would lose, which a VLM can then reason over directly**

\(C\) Document pages cannot be embedded or retrieved at all

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Describe, in 4-5 sentences, a scenario from your own domain where retrieving a document's image/page (not just its text) would meaningfully improve an answer, and why.

**Lecture 491 Building a multimodal pipeline hands-on**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Build a working multimodal pipeline that accepts an image and a text query and produces a grounded answer using a vision-language model.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Teacher explanation** | This hands-on lecture walks through assembling a minimal multimodal pipeline end to end: loading a pretrained vision-language model, preprocessing an input image into the format the model's vision encoder expects (typically resizing and normalizing pixel values), formatting a text query alongside the image per the model's expected input template, and running inference to produce a text answer grounded in the image. Practical details matter here in ways that are easy to overlook: image preprocessing steps (resize dimensions, normalization values) must exactly match what the model was trained with, or outputs degrade silently without any error being thrown, and the prompt template connecting image and text tokens is typically model-specific, so copying a prompt format from a different model's documentation produces broken or nonsensical outputs. Building this pipeline with a few test images spanning different content types (a photo, a chart, a document page) is a good way to surface these integration issues early, since a pipeline that works perfectly on one test image can silently fail on another due to a preprocessing mismatch that only shows up with certain image characteristics. Once a basic pipeline runs reliably across a handful of varied test images, it becomes the foundation that Lecture 492's evaluation methodology and the multimodal document assistant project both build directly on top of. |
| **Worked example**      | A learner builds a pipeline that correctly answers questions about a product photo but produces garbled nonsense on a screenshot of a spreadsheet, eventually tracing the bug to an image resize step that distorted the spreadsheet's small text beyond recognition while barely affecting the product photo.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

**Knowledge check:** Why is testing a multimodal pipeline on several different image content types important rather than testing on just one?

\(A\) Testing on one image type is always sufficient to guarantee a pipeline works universally

**(B) A preprocessing mismatch can silently degrade results on certain image characteristics while appearing to work fine on others, so varied test images surface integration bugs that a single test case would miss**

\(C\) Multimodal pipelines cannot process more than one image type by design

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Build a minimal multimodal pipeline using an available vision-language model or API, and run it on at least 3 different image types (a photo, a chart or table, and a document page), recording any failures or odd outputs.

**Lecture 492 Evaluating multimodal model outputs**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Design an evaluation approach for multimodal outputs that checks genuine visual grounding rather than plausible-sounding text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
