| **Teacher explanation** | Evaluating multimodal outputs is harder than evaluating text-only outputs because a multimodal model's response can look fluent and plausible while being completely ungrounded in the actual image -- so evaluation must specifically verify that the stated visual claims are true of the particular image shown, not just that the response reads well. A practical evaluation approach involves building a test set where each image has specific, checkable ground-truth facts attached (exact counts, specific colors, specific text visible in the image, specific spatial relationships), then scoring the model's outputs against those specific facts rather than against a vague overall-quality judgment, since specific checkable facts expose grounding failures that a general quality rating would miss entirely. It's also valuable to deliberately include adversarial test cases -- images where an obvious, generic answer would be wrong for this specific image -- since a model that isn't truly grounded will often default to the generic, commonly-seen answer rather than the one true of this image, and such cases are far more diagnostic of genuine visual grounding than easy, typical images. Combining checkable-fact scoring with these harder adversarial test cases gives a much more honest picture of whether a multimodal model (or pipeline) is reasoning over the actual image content versus pattern-matching to generic plausible-sounding answers. |
| **Worked example**      | An evaluation set includes a photo of a red stop sign that's unusually faded to pale pink; a model that answers "red" by default pattern-matching rather than actually looking fails this specific adversarial test case, revealing weak visual grounding that an easy, typical stop-sign image wouldn't have exposed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

**Knowledge check:** Why are adversarial test cases, where the generic expected answer is wrong for a specific image, especially useful for evaluating multimodal grounding?

\(A\) Adversarial cases are only useful for text-only models, not multimodal ones

**(B) They expose whether a model defaults to generic pattern-matched answers rather than genuinely reasoning over the actual image shown, which typical easy images would not reveal**

\(C\) Adversarial cases make models perform better automatically without any other changes

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Build a small evaluation set of 5 images with specific checkable facts (counts, colors, text, spatial relationships) attached, including at least 1 deliberately adversarial case, and score a multimodal model's outputs against those facts.

**Lecture 493 Common multimodal failure modes**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Identify and characterize recurring multimodal failure modes: misreading visual details and hallucinating content not present in the image.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Teacher explanation** | Two failure modes recur across nearly all current multimodal systems and are worth naming precisely so they can be diagnosed rather than vaguely described as 'the model got it wrong.' Misreading visual details means the model attends to the wrong region, miscounts objects, misreads small or low-contrast text, or confuses visually similar elements -- this is fundamentally a perception failure, where the model genuinely processed the image but extracted the wrong detail from it, and it's especially common with small text, dense tables, unusual angles, or low image resolution. Hallucinating content not in the image is a distinct and arguably more concerning failure mode: the model confidently describes objects, text, or details that simply are not present in the image at all, typically because its language-model component is pattern-matching to what's statistically likely to appear in a similar-looking scene rather than being constrained strictly by what the vision encoder actually detected -- for instance describing a 'cup of coffee on the table' in a kitchen photo that contains no cup at all, because kitchen photos statistically often contain cups. Distinguishing these two failure modes matters for mitigation: misreading is often improved with higher-resolution image inputs or explicit prompting to look carefully at a specific region, while hallucination is better mitigated by grounding techniques, lower generation temperature, and evaluation specifically designed to catch confidently-stated false visual claims, as covered in Lecture 492. |
| **Worked example**      | A model describing a conference room photo confidently mentions "a laptop open on the table," but careful inspection shows no laptop is actually present anywhere in the image -- the model's language component filled in a statistically plausible object that conference-room photos commonly contain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Knowledge check:** What distinguishes hallucination from misreading as multimodal failure modes?

\(A\) They are the same failure mode described with two different names

**(B) Misreading extracts the wrong detail from content that is genuinely present, while hallucination confidently states content that is not present in the image at all**

\(C\) Hallucination only occurs in text-only models, never in multimodal ones

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Find or create 3 test images, run them through a multimodal model with a request to describe the scene in detail, and identify at least one instance of either misreading or hallucination in the outputs, explaining which failure mode it is and why.

**Lecture 494 Cost and latency considerations specific to multimodal models**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Analyze why multimodal models carry different cost and latency profiles than text-only models and plan deployment decisions around those differences.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Teacher explanation** | Multimodal models typically cost more per request and respond more slowly than equivalent text-only models, for a concrete architectural reason: an image, once encoded into tokens by the vision encoder (recall Lecture 487's patch-token approach), often contributes hundreds of additional tokens to the model's input sequence even for a single moderate-resolution image, and since compute cost in a transformer scales with sequence length, this directly increases both the per-request cost and the processing latency compared to a text-only query of similar length. Higher-resolution images make this worse: finer-grained image encoding (more patches, to preserve detail needed for reading small text or counting many objects) directly means more image tokens and proportionally higher cost and latency, creating a direct tradeoff between visual detail and request cost that text-only systems simply don't face. Practical mitigation strategies include: downsampling images to the minimum resolution the task actually requires (over-sending high resolution for a task that doesn't need fine detail wastes cost for no benefit), batching multiple images efficiently rather than one request per image where the task allows, and caching results for images that are queried repeatedly rather than re-processing identical visual content on every request. Planning for this cost and latency reality up front -- rather than discovering it only after a multimodal feature is already deployed at scale -- is a routine part of deciding whether and how to deploy a multimodal system in production. |
| **Worked example**      | A document-processing system that initially sent full-resolution scans (each costing hundreds of extra image tokens) cuts its per-request cost substantially by downsampling scans to the minimum resolution still sufficient for reading the document's text accurately.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Knowledge check:** Why does a higher-resolution image input directly increase both the cost and latency of a multimodal model request?

\(A\) Resolution has no effect on token count or compute cost in multimodal models

**(B) Finer-grained image encoding produces more image tokens, and transformer compute cost scales with sequence length, so higher resolution directly increases tokens, cost, and latency**

\(C\) Higher resolution images are always processed by a completely separate, unrelated model

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** For a multimodal use case of your choice, estimate roughly how image resolution choices would affect token count and cost, and propose one specific mitigation strategy to reduce cost without sacrificing task accuracy.

**Lecture 495 Responsible use considerations specific to vision and multimodal AI**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Identify responsible-AI considerations unique to vision and multimodal systems, building on Year 1 Month 7 and previewing Month 30.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Teacher explanation** | Year 1 Month 7 introduced responsible AI broadly -- bias, fairness, and transparency concerns applicable to any AI system. Vision and multimodal AI raise several additional considerations specific to processing visual content: images can contain personally identifiable information (faces, license plates, visible documents) that text rarely carries in the same direct way, so a multimodal system processing user-submitted images needs explicit policies about what visual information it should and shouldn't extract, store, or act on, separate from its text-handling policies. Multimodal systems can also exhibit visual bias specifically: performing less accurately on images of people from underrepresented demographic groups, under certain lighting conditions, or with certain cultural dress or contexts not well represented in training data, which is a distinct failure pattern from the text-based bias Month 7 covered and requires its own targeted bias auditing using diverse test images, not an assumption that text-bias mitigation techniques automatically transfer. Finally, multimodal hallucination (Lecture 493) carries sharper real-world risk than text hallucination in some high-stakes visual tasks -- a hallucinated detail in a medical image description or a security-camera analysis isn't just an inconvenience but can directly drive a harmful downstream decision -- which is why responsible deployment of multimodal systems in such high-stakes domains needs human review processes specifically designed around this risk, a theme Month 30's AI safety content develops much further. |
| **Worked example**      | A hiring-related photo-screening tool found to perform noticeably less accurately on images of people with certain skin tones or hairstyles exemplifies visual bias specific to multimodal systems, distinct from the text-based fairness metrics Year 2 Month 14 covered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

**Knowledge check:** What is one responsible-AI consideration that arises specifically from processing visual content, beyond the text-based concerns Year 1 Month 7 covered?

\(A\) Visual content carries no privacy or bias considerations distinct from text

**(B) Images can carry direct personally identifiable information like faces, and multimodal systems can show visual bias across demographic groups or lighting conditions not well represented in training data**

\(C\) Responsible AI concerns apply only to text-only systems, never to visual or multimodal ones

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Write 4-5 sentences describing one specific responsible-use risk unique to a vision or multimodal system you could imagine deploying, and one concrete mitigation you would put in place before deployment.

**Lecture 496 Multimodal document assistant project, part 1: ingestion and retrieval**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Begin the capstone project by building a document ingestion and multimodal retrieval pipeline over a small collection of real documents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Teacher explanation** | This lecture begins the month's capstone: the multimodal document assistant, a system that can answer questions grounded in a small collection of real documents containing text, tables, and visual elements like charts or diagrams, applying this month's concepts end to end. Part 1 covers ingestion and retrieval: collect or select 10-20 real documents containing a mix of text, tables, and at least some charts or images (reports, manuals, or similar), process each document page preserving both its text and its layout per Lecture 489's document-understanding approach, generate multimodal embeddings for each page (or relevant page regions) per Lecture 490's multimodal RAG pattern, and store them in a vector database ready for retrieval. The goal of this first part is a working retrieval step you can test in isolation: given a sample query, confirm the system retrieves the actually-relevant page or pages from your document collection, checking this across several varied test queries before moving on to generation, since a retrieval step that silently returns irrelevant pages will undermine every answer downstream no matter how good the generation step is. Keep your document set small and well-understood at this stage specifically so that you, as the project's builder, can manually verify whether each retrieval result is actually correct -- this manual verification becomes far harder, though still necessary in principle, once a document collection grows large. |
| **Worked example**      | A learner collects 15 PDF product manuals with embedded diagrams, embeds each page using a multimodal embedding model, and tests retrieval with the query "what does the warning symbol on page 4 of the router manual mean," confirming the system retrieves that exact page before moving to the generation step.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Knowledge check:** What is the primary goal of part 1 of the multimodal document assistant project?

\(A\) A fully polished, user-facing interface with no further evaluation needed

**(B) A working, manually-verifiable retrieval step that reliably returns relevant document pages for varied test queries, as groundwork for the generation step**

\(C\) Training an entirely new vision-language model from scratch

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Complete part 1 of your multimodal document assistant: ingest 10-20 real documents with mixed text/table/visual content, build multimodal embeddings and retrieval, and verify retrieval correctness on at least 5 varied test queries.

**Lecture 497 Multimodal document assistant project, part 2: generation and evaluation**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Complete the capstone project by connecting retrieval to a vision-language model for answer generation, then evaluating the full pipeline for grounding and failure modes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Teacher explanation** | Part 2 completes the project by connecting your part-1 retrieval step to a vision-language model following Lecture 491's pipeline pattern: retrieved pages (as images, preserving layout) plus the user's query are passed into the VLM, which generates a grounded answer, and the full retrieval-plus-generation pipeline is tested end to end on your original test queries plus several new ones. Evaluation of the completed pipeline should apply Lecture 492's checkable-fact approach specifically: for each test query, verify not just that an answer was produced, but that its specific claims (numbers, labels, described visual details) are actually true of the retrieved document content, and deliberately include a few adversarial or edge-case queries (a question about a detail that looks similar to something common but is actually different in your specific documents) to probe for the hallucination and misreading failure modes from Lecture 493. The project concludes with a short written assessment covering what fraction of test queries were answered correctly and grounded, what failure modes appeared and in what proportion, and what you would change with more time -- better retrieval, a different VLM, or image preprocessing fixes -- mirroring the kind of honest pipeline assessment a real team would produce before considering such a system for real document workflows. This structured failure-mode analysis, rather than a single aggregate accuracy number, is what actually tells you whether and how the system is ready to be trusted. |
| **Worked example**      | After testing the full pipeline on 20 queries, a learner finds 16 correctly grounded, 3 showing minor misreading of small table text, and 1 showing outright hallucination of a chart value not present in the source page, and recommends higher-resolution page images as the next fix.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

**Knowledge check:** Why does the project's final assessment emphasize a breakdown of specific failure modes rather than a single aggregate accuracy number?

\(A\) A single aggregate number always provides enough information to decide whether a system is ready for real use

**(B) Breaking down which specific failure modes occurred, and how often, tells you what to actually fix next, which an aggregate accuracy number alone cannot reveal**

\(C\) Failure mode analysis is purely optional busywork with no bearing on whether to trust the system

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Complete part 2 of your project: connect retrieval to a VLM for generation, run the full pipeline on at least 10 test queries including 2 adversarial ones, and write a short assessment covering accuracy, specific failure modes observed, and your top recommended fix.

**Lecture 498 Multimodal systems in context: a project retrospective**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Synthesize the month's concepts by articulating, for your own completed project, the key architectural and evaluation decisions and their consequences.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Teacher explanation** | This retrospective asks you to step back from the mechanics of embeddings, VLMs, and retrieval pipelines, and instead articulate the decision chain behind your multimodal document assistant: why multimodal retrieval (retrieving whole pages as images) was chosen over text-only extraction for your document set, what tradeoffs in cost and latency (Lecture 494) your design accepted, and what your failure-mode evaluation from Lecture 497 actually revealed about where the system is and isn't trustworthy yet. Frame this retrospective, as in Month 28's equivalent exercise, for a non-technical stakeholder deciding whether to invest further: state what documents and queries the system handles well, what specific failure modes appeared and how often, what responsible-use considerations from Lecture 495 would need addressing before any real deployment (especially if the documents might contain sensitive personal information), and a clear recommendation about readiness. Being specific and honest about limitations here -- rather than presenting only the system's successes -- is exactly the discipline that separates a genuinely useful retrospective from a sales pitch, and it's a discipline worth carrying into every real multimodal system you build after this course, since multimodal failure modes in particular are often invisible until someone specifically looks for them. |
| **Worked example**      | A learner's retrospective states: 'We retrieve whole pages as images rather than text alone because our manuals contain diagrams critical to meaning; this costs more per query due to image tokens, which we mitigated by downsampling; evaluation found 80% fully grounded answers with hallucination appearing mainly on queries about small chart values, so I'd recommend a pilot with human review on chart-related answers specifically, not full automation yet.'                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

**Knowledge check:** What should a project retrospective prioritize over simply reporting successes?

\(A\) Omitting any mention of limitations so the project appears maximally successful

**(B) Being specific and honest about which failure modes appeared, how often, and what would need addressing before real deployment**

\(C\) Retrospectives should focus exclusively on the underlying model architecture with no reference to evaluation results

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Write a 150-250 word retrospective of your multimodal document assistant project in the stakeholder-facing style described, covering retrieval design, cost tradeoffs, evaluation findings, responsible-use considerations, and a clear recommendation.

**Lecture 499 Multimodal AI: connecting back to embeddings, RAG, and agents**

*Year 3 · Month 29 · Computer Vision + Multimodal AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Articulate how this month's multimodal concepts extend and connect to Month 26's RAG and Month 27's agent architectures.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Teacher explanation** | This lecture closes the month by explicitly connecting multimodal AI back to the two preceding months rather than treating it as an isolated topic: multimodal RAG (Lecture 490) is a direct extension of Month 26's text-based RAG, replacing or augmenting text-chunk retrieval with image and page-level retrieval while keeping the same core retrieve-then-generate structure, and multimodal embeddings are simply a shared vector space spanning more than one modality rather than a different retrieval paradigm altogether. The connection to Month 27's agents is equally direct: an agent (as covered in Month 27) that can call tools and reason over multiple steps can be given a multimodal document-retrieval tool exactly like it would be given any other tool, meaning the multimodal document assistant built this month could become one capability of a larger agent that also searches the web, calls APIs, or performs calculations, rather than being a standalone system that must handle every kind of request on its own. Seeing multimodal AI this way -- as an extension of concepts already mastered, rather than a wholly separate discipline -- is the right mental model heading toward Month 30, since many of the responsible-AI and red-teaming concerns there (such as hallucination and failure-mode testing) apply to multimodal and agentic systems in essentially the same structural way they applied to the text-only systems covered earlier in this program. |
| **Worked example**      | An agent built in Month 27's style could be extended with a new tool, "search_documents(query)", that internally runs this month's multimodal retrieval pipeline and returns a grounded, image-aware answer, making the agent capable of answering questions about scanned documents without any change to the agent's core reasoning loop.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

**Knowledge check:** How does multimodal retrieval relate structurally to the text-based RAG covered in Month 26?

\(A\) Multimodal retrieval is a completely unrelated paradigm sharing no structure with text-based RAG

**(B) Multimodal RAG keeps the same retrieve-then-generate structure as text-based RAG, simply extending retrieval to span images and document pages within a shared embedding space**

\(C\) RAG and multimodal retrieval can never be combined within the same system

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Write 4-5 sentences describing how you would add your multimodal document assistant as a tool inside a Month-27-style agent, including what new tool description and inputs the agent would need to call it correctly.

**Lecture 501 AI safety as a technical field, beyond introductory responsible AI**

*Year 3 · Month 30 · AI Safety + Responsible AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Distinguish AI safety as a technical discipline from Year 1 Month 7's introductory responsible-AI content, framing the field's core concerns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Teacher explanation** | Year 1 Month 7 introduced responsible AI at an awareness level: recognizing that bias, transparency, and misuse are things a practitioner should care about. AI safety, as a technical field, goes further by treating these concerns as engineering problems with methods, metrics, and testable interventions -- it asks specifically how to systematically find a system's failure modes before deployment (red-teaming), how to measure whether a system behaves as intended under adversarial conditions (robustness testing), how to verify a system's outputs can be trusted in high-stakes settings (explainability and evaluation), and how to respond when something goes wrong anyway (incident response). This technical framing matters because it shifts AI safety from a values statement into a concrete practice with deliverables: a red-team report documenting discovered failure modes, a guardrail test suite with pass/fail criteria, a documented risk assessment, and an incident response plan are all tangible artifacts a team can produce and review, not abstract principles. For the specific case of modern LLMs and agents (Months 25-27), AI safety work concentrates heavily on adversarial robustness -- can the system be manipulated into unintended behavior through crafted inputs -- precisely because these systems follow natural-language instructions, which creates a much larger and more creative attack surface than older, narrower machine learning systems had. |
| **Worked example**      | A team shipping an LLM-powered agent treats 'be responsible' as a starting value, but AI safety as a practice means they also produce a red-team report listing 12 discovered prompt-injection vulnerabilities, a guardrail test suite that automatically re-checks those 12 cases on every code change, and a written incident response plan for if a 13th is found in production.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

**Knowledge check:** How does AI safety as a technical field differ from the introductory responsible-AI awareness covered in Year 1 Month 7?

\(A\) They are identical, with AI safety just being a renamed version of the same content

**(B) AI safety treats responsible-AI concerns as engineering problems with concrete methods and testable deliverables, such as red-team reports and guardrail test suites, not just values awareness**

\(C\) AI safety only applies to narrow, non-generative machine learning systems

***Correct answer: B***

**Homework:** Write 4-5 sentences describing one concrete, testable AI-safety deliverable (not just a stated value) you could produce for a system you've built or imagined in this program.

**Lecture 502 Red-teaming an AI system: systematic failure-mode probing**

*Year 3 · Month 30 · AI Safety + Responsible AI · 1 guided hour + homework*

|                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Learning outcome**    | Design and run a structured red-teaming exercise that systematically probes an LLM or agent system for failure modes rather than testing ad hoc.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Teacher explanation** | Red-teaming means deliberately and systematically trying to make a system fail, rather than only testing the inputs it's expected to handle well -- for an LLM or agent (Months 25-27), this means probing categories like: getting it to produce disallowed content, getting it to reveal information it shouldn't, getting it to take an unintended action if it has tool access, and getting it to contradict its own stated instructions or guardrails. The word 'systematic' is doing real work here: effective red-teaming works through a structured taxonomy of attack categories (rather than randomly trying things), documents each attempted attack and its outcome whether it succeeded or failed, and tracks a running list of confirmed vulnerabilities with enough detail (exact input, exact problematic output) that each one can be turned into a regression test later, which is exactly what feeds Lecture 505's automated guardrail test suite. Red-teaming an agent specifically requires extra categories beyond a plain chat LLM: does a crafted input cause the agent to call a tool it shouldn't, with parameters it shouldn't, or in a sequence that produces a harmful combined effect even if each individual tool call looks reasonable in isolation. Treating red-teaming as a structured, documented, repeatable process -- not a one-time informal poke at the system -- is what turns it from an interesting exercise into a genuine safety practice that compounds in value over time as the documented findings get reused. |
